definition: There is one of these for each product the business sells, for each ingredient or packaging item it buys to make one, and for each product definition that only groups related sizes and packs. Everything else about a product refers back to it: what it is made from, what it must be, how long it lasts and what its pack says are each kept in their own concept. It is not a batch, which is one production run of a product, and it is not the facts that only a consumer goods product has, which the product's consumer goods definition holds.
distinct_need: Holds the identity of every product, sold or bought in; no other concept in the model does.

definition: There is one of these for each identifier a product is known by, in each scheme, such as a trade item number or the organisation's own material number. It is not the name of the product, which belongs to the product itself, and it is not an identifier of an organisation, which belongs to the legal entity identifiers.

definition: There is one of these for each allergen a product declares in a market, either because it contains the allergen or because the allergen may be present. The allergen is a value from the list for that market, so a product sold in two markets has an entry for each. You can rely on it to say which allergens are declared, whether each is contained or only may be present, how each came to be associated with the product, and whether it is known only because a supplier said so; for a product made from other products, the contained allergens come from its formulation. It is not the production line or the factory that cross-contact arises in, which belong to the manufacturing model.
distinct_need: Holds the declared allergens of a product, whether each is contained or may be present, and where each comes from, which no other concept does.
